full_judgment: 12. In a bid to deal with the issue of non-production of the relevant papers of the LA Case No. 77 of 1963-64 at the trial Court, he places section 114(g) of the Evidence Act and also refers to the case of M Saeed Sehgal vs Kazi Khurshid Hasan 17 DLR (SC) 111, wherein it was held that "plaintiff not calling for the accounts which were available and within his reach, presumption is to be drawn against him". He submits that the said Plot No. 41 cannot be included in the said Gazette Notification dated 4-3-1965 published in connection with under LA Case No. 77 of 1963-64 by a mere amendment of the aforesaid original Gazette Notification inasmuch as the said LA Case No. 77 of 1963-64 was initiated and, finally, ended up under the (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act, 1984, and the said Act being dead from the year 1982, inclusion of the said Plot No. 41 in 2010 showing the same as an acquired land under LA Case No 77 of 1963-64 under the said Act is illegal and, on the other hand, the provisions of the Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Ordinance, 1982 also cannot be applied in publishing the said notice as the case land was not acquired under the Ordinance of 1982. Mr Khalilur Rahman, the learned advocate for the petitioner, then, refers to the case of Osimuddin vs Bangladesh reported in 1 BLC (1996) 375 and, under paragraph 9 of the said judgment, it was held that "in the absence of notification published in the official Gazette as required under sections 4 and 6 of the Forest Act, 1927 the suit land cannot be vested in the Government through Forest Department as the departmental notification cannot affect the right of the public". Thus he submits that since the government did not include Plot No. 41 in the Gazette Notification dated 4-3-1965 finally published in connection with LA Case No. 77 of 1963-64, the right and title of the petitioner's predecessors remained unaffected and their names in SA Khatian No. 1687 remained valid. As such, while they were lawfully owning and possessing the case land upon paying rents/taxes to the government, and they validly transferred the same to the petitioner through other purchases who also got their names mutated in the government record (Annexure A series).
